output.summary: The project team aimed to reduce the production cost of a remote control from 25 Euros to 12.50 Euros. They replaced kinetic energy with normal batteries, saving costs. The Industrial Designer simplified the shape from a double curve to a single curve. To further cut expenses, the team removed the number buttons one through nine, saving 4.50 Euros, and later decided to drop the speech recognition feature, saving an additional 4 Euros. Despite the cost implications, they retained the LCD screen, which was more popular than speech recognition according to Marketing data. The final design featured a single-curved, hard plastic casing with a special color and one integrated scroll-wheel push-button. The remote control was named 'The Real Remote.' During evaluations, the team rated the design’s match to young user behavior as a 3/7, visibility of relevant functions as a 5/7, technological innovation as a 2/7, and ease of use as a 6/7, resulting in an overall score of approximately 3.11. The team noted significant improvements in collaboration after the first meeting and agreed there was room for creativity within financial constraints. They found the digital pen more effective for their work than the Smartboard screen.
